task.name: Ratified semantic readiness: review policy, operator ratification, and REVIEWED_READY admission land as one contract
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2685
---

## What

Ratified semantic readiness: the policy that decides when a semantic evaluation is required,
how an operator ratifies its outcome, and how that ratified state — never raw model output —
produces `REVIEWED_READY` and is consumed by sprint admission.

This is the second half of slice 6 of the typed intake contract (#2724). #2685 builds the
evaluator as an audit-only instrument that changes nothing. This issue decides what its output
is allowed to mean, and wires it.

## Why

`REVIEWED_READY` is the milestone's missing state — capture → shaped → groomed → **ready** —
and nothing today produces it. But the decisions that produce it are policy, not mechanism, and
each one is a place where a wrong default is worse than no state at all:

- A clean evaluation that becomes ready on its own gives an unratified probabilistic outcome
  the authority of a factual claim. ADR-0009 clause 6 forbids exactly that: admission consumes a
  recorded, operator-ratified state, never model output directly.
- A ratification that survives an edit to the document it was made against asserts readiness
  about text nobody reviewed.
- An evaluation that completes late and restores a superseded state reproduces the defect
  #2666 documents one layer up, where an earlier verdict lands after a later one and wins.

Splitting these from the evaluator is deliberate. #2685 produces the evidence — known-defect
recovery, human-confirmed precision, repeat stability, cost per confirmed finding, and novel
defects beyond a frozen human baseline. These decisions should be made against that evidence
rather than in advance of it.

This issue is captured as a draft on purpose. It becomes runnable only when the operator records
a decision to proceed against #2685's measurements; if the evaluator does not earn its place,
this is closed unbuilt. That gate is a commitment decision, not something a dev can satisfy.

## Acceptance criteria

- Policy names which types and states require a semantic evaluation before implementation, and
  states what happens to every type it does not name.
- A clean evaluation does not by itself produce `REVIEWED_READY`. Readiness follows an operator
  ratification recorded against the exact revision that was evaluated.
- Accepting a raised concern and rejecting one both have a stated outcome. A rejected concern
  passes without further challenge on the same revision; an accepted one withholds readiness for
  that revision until the document changes.
- A ratification names the revision it was made against, and a document whose revision changes
  no longer reports as ready on the strength of it.
- An evaluation that completes after a newer revision exists never restores readiness for the
  revision it read.
- Sprint admission consumes the ratified state and never raw model output. A document carrying
  concerns that no operator has ratified is not refused on their account.
- A document with no recorded evaluation reports as unevaluated rather than as ready or refused,
  and whether that withholds admission follows the policy above rather than a default chosen
  here.
- The structural verdict is unchanged by everything in this issue. A defect this stage catches
  produces a concern, never a new structural rule.

## Example

```
groom 2681            -> RUNNABLE                (structural, unchanged throughout)
evaluate 2681         -> 4 concerns   revision=r1
admission 2681        -> not ready — concerns unratified

operator ratifies: 3 accepted, 1 rejected  (recorded against r1)
admission 2681        -> not ready — 3 accepted concerns withhold readiness at r1

author edits the body -> revision r2
admission 2681        -> unevaluated at r2; the r1 ratification no longer speaks for it
```

A late evaluation of `r1` arriving after `r2` exists changes nothing.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 collapses policy applicability into semantic evaluation status: it defines not_required as the reported status for every unnamed type/state. The acceptance criterion requires every document lacking an evaluation record to report unevaluated, with the separate policy decision determining whether that absence withholds admission. As written, an implementation-ready-exempt document with no record would report not_required rather than unevaluated.
  Suggestion: Model separate axes in src/theforge/eval/semantic_readiness.py: an evaluation state that is unevaluated whenever no current-digest record exists, and a policy requirement of required or not_required. Derive admission from both axes, and add a Step 6 test proving a no-record, policy-exempt document reports unevaluated while retaining its existing structural/lifecycle admission result.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 offers two alternatives for the manifest path — a shared boundary reached by both query and manifest modes, or an equivalent manifest admission pass before run_sprint consumes {issue: N} entries (src/theforge/sprint/manifest.py:185-189, expanded around line 388) — without choosing one. The two differ in blast radius: cli/sprint.py resolves manifest slugs through parse_manifest_story_refs (src/theforge/cli/sprint.py:305-306) before run_sprint, so the insertion point is not obvious.
  Suggestion: Have the dev pick the shared-boundary form (one derivation function called from apply_shape_gate, the manifest issue-expansion path, and build_ready_queue) and record where the manifest-side call lands, so the seam test in Step 6 asserts a single agreed decision point rather than two parallel implementations.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 also leaves the skip-emission shape as an either/or (new SkippedIssue.source vs. existing source plus semantic reason codes). SkippedIssue.source is documented as 'label' or 'local_check' (src/theforge/sprint/shape_gate.py:88) and flows into skip_report.py (lines 55-57, 109, 141) plus substrate payloads (shape_gate.py:458, 506, 524) and the taxonomy classifier, which derives category from code + source.
  Suggestion: Choose the reuse-existing-source-with-semantic-reason-codes option unless a new source is required; if a new source is introduced, update all three consumers listed above in the same step and assert the taxonomy category in tests/test_skip_taxonomy.py.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 requires --force not to bypass semantic withholding, but the force branch (src/theforge/sprint/shape_gate.py:529-542) currently rebuilds runnable from all skips with only the operator-action exclusion. The plan does not say how semantically-withheld issues are identified in that rebuild.
  Suggestion: Track semantically-withheld issue numbers in a set alongside operator_action_label_numbers and exclude both in the force_runnable comprehension; the Step 6 force test should cover all four withholding states.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Stated risk 1 (the draft gate: proceeding requires the operator's recorded decision against #2685's measurements) is carried by design — Step 0 is a human confirmation the dev agent cannot satisfy or verify, and preflight raised the same warning.
  Suggestion: Confirm the recorded proceed decision on the issue before dev budget is assigned; no code change is needed, and the gate must stay out of runtime policy as Step 0 states.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Stated risk 2 (input_digest ignores metadata-only edits) is retired for the ACs — the digest covers title, body, and canonical_type (src/theforge/eval/semantic_input.py:27-34), so label changes that alter canonical type do invalidate a ratification — but the residual case, a label edit that does not change canonical_type, is only documented, not tested.
  Suggestion: Add one Step 6 case asserting that a non-canonical label change leaves the ratification valid, so the documented boundary is pinned rather than implied.

finding_registry.description: When forge sprint --force encounters semantic readiness skips, the command prints that all issues are running anyway even though the shape gate has removed the semantically withheld issues from the runnable set.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
